title: Orchestrated Auto-Remediation Pipeline with Trace Fabric and Slack Ops Briefs
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: We still spend a large fraction of oncall time on routine mitigation tasks (eg. restart worker group, rotate cache, scale replica set) that are safe to automate for known failure classes. Current triggers live in disparate places (PagerDuty alerts, Grafana alerts, CloudWatch metrics) and lack a single canonical trace-linked context. This ticket implements an orchestrated auto-remediation pipeline that: 1) consumes deduplicated incident signals, 2) attaches a lightweight trace fabric snapshot and correlated logs, 3) evaluates an automation policy, 4) executes safe remediation actions behind a human-in-loop approval when necessary, and 5) posts a structured Ops Brief to Slack and creates a draft postmortem if criteria are met.
motivation: Reduce mean time to mitigation for repeatable failure modes, reduce oncall cognitive load, and create a reproducible evidence chain for automation decisions to feed regressions and postmortems. Provide guaranteed audit trail and kill-switch for automations for enterprise customers (Private/Dedicated).
goals: 1) Ship initial automation rules for 3 winner use-cases (model-serving OOM/eviction, persistent KV cache misses causing latency spikes, GPU driver crash loop). 2) Build trace fabric snapshot API for quick context snapshot and attach to PagerDuty/Slack artifacts. 3) Create Slack interactive Ops Brief with one-click rollback/approve buttons and one-tap runbook link. 4) Ensure idempotent, auditable remediation runs with CB/ratelimit and operator overrides.
non_goals: Full SRE playbook authoring UI (will integrate with existing runbook store), complex cross-service transaction orchestration, or automatically applying experimental kernel changes without manual review.
design_notes:
- Signal ingestion: central 'incident-fabric' consumer will normalize events from PD, Prometheus/Grafana alerts, and runtime traces. Use an LRU deduper keyed by (service, signature, window) to collapse noisy duplicates.
- Trace fabric: use a lightweight sampled span bundle (top 3 spans by latency + 200ms window capture) + relevant LogQL query snapshot. Stored in encrypted object store with short TTL and attached by reference.
- Decision engine: policy language (YAML) with thresholds, safeties, and required approvals. Policy evaluator runs in sandboxed lambda with strict timeouts and immutability.
- Remediation executor: idempotent command runner that requires action tokens; remote operations are logged to KMS-backed audit trail. Introduce circuit-breaker that halts automation if upstream error rate rises or if more than 1% of automations produce a rollback in 24h.
- Slack integration: structured Ops Brief message posted to #ops-incident with buttons: Approve Remediation, Rollback Remediation, Open Runbook, Create Draft Postmortem. Buttons call back to a secured endpoint with signed tokens.
- PagerDuty: Attach short summary + link to Ops Brief + trace fabric reference. If automation is applied, add a PD annotation and update incident lifecycle metadata.
tradeoffs:
- Full automation vs human control: default to conservative human-in-loop for first 3 cases to collect metrics and trust signals.
- Trace fidelity vs cost: snapshotting only top spans and sampled logs to balance storage and retrieval speed.
- Centralized decision engine increases blast radius if compromised; mitigate with sandboxing and strict RBAC + KMS signing.
acceptance_criteria: Automation chain fully exercised in staging for 3 targeted failure modes with end-to-end telemetry and no silent failures
Ops Brief Slack message contains trace fabric link, runbook link, and functional approve/rollback buttons (integration e2e test passing)
PagerDuty incidents annotated with automation actions and link back to Ops Brief for all test incidents
Every remediation execution is recorded in audit log with KMS-signed provenance and can be queried via Console within 15s
Circuit-breaker prevents further automations when rollback ratio > 1% within 24 hours in canary cohort
Playbook for disabling automations and emergency rollback is documented and accessible to oncall
Security review completed and penetration testing for callback endpoints passed
tasks: Spec: policy YAML schema and evaluator contract
Build: trace fabric snapshot API + storage + SDK helper
Build: remediation executor with idempotency and audit logging
Integrate: Slack Ops Brief message templates and interactivity endpoints
Integrate: PagerDuty annotations and incident metadata mapping
Tests: staging e2e for 3 failure modes and canary in prod for low-traffic customer
Docs: runbook updates and runbook-store integration notes
Security: threat model + key management + external pentest
implementation_notes:
- Use existing telemetry-ingest queue (kafka-topic: telemetry.events) and extend with a new consumer group 'incident-fabric'.
- Reuse existing trace-collector APIs but add lightweight 'snapshot' endpoint to avoid full trace rehydration.
- Slack messages will use signed callback tokens rotated monthly and verified using KMS public keys.
- Add new Console UI widget to show recent automated actions with filters (service, rule, outcome).
risks: Automation causing unintended state changes if idempotency is imperfect
Increased alert storm surface if deduping is incorrect
Security exposure from interactive endpoints if token signing or key rotation fails
Customer trust risk for enterprise customers if automations run without clear audit trail
rollout_plan: 1) Internal staging runbook: enable automation for synthetic tests only. 2) Canary: enable for 10% of low-risk production traffic with human-in-loop approvals. 3) Expand to 50% after 2 weeks with monitored SLOs. 4) Full enablement for these three policies after 30 days if success metrics met. Each step gated by checklist including security sign-off and runbook owner approval.
postmortem_policy: If an automation causes an incident with severity >= Sev2, automatically create a draft postmortem in /incidents/drafts with attached trace fabric and remediation logs and notify the incident commander. Runbook owners are assigned for follow-up.
